question.worked_solution:
We must factor the quadratic expression

$$
5{h}^{2}-12h-9.
$$

First, we find two numbers that 

- multiply to the product of the quadratic coefficient and the constant ($5\times -9=-45$), and

- add to the linear coefficient ($-12$).

The factor pairs of $-45$ are

$$
(1,-45),\,\,(-1,45),\,\,(3,-15),\,\,(-3,15),\,\,(5,-9),\,\,(-5,9).
$$

Notice the numbers in the factor pair $(3,-15)$ add to $-12:$ 

$$
3-15=-12\,✓
$$

Then, rewrite the linear term as $3h-15h,$ and factor the result by grouping:

$$
\begin{aligned}5{h}^{2}-12h-9 & = \\ 5{h}^{2}+3h-15h-9 & = \\ 5{h}^{2}-15h+3h-9 & = \\ (5{h}^{2}-15h)+(3h-9) & = \\ 5h(h-3)+3(h-3) & = \\ (5h+3)(h-3) & \end{aligned}
$$
